exposure: crystalloid preload (15 ml/kg ringer lactates solution over 20 minutes prior to spinal block)
prompt crystalloid administration post induction of spinal anesthesia (ringer lactate over 20 min post CSF tapping)
cohort: One hundred and fifty-four women undergoing elective caesarian section under spinal anesthesia.
finding: Crystalloid preload resulted in more nausea, vomiting, and hypotension compared to prompt administration post induction of spinal anesthesia in women undergoing elective caesarian section.
mod_finding: Crystalloid preload during elective caesarean section was associated with higher rates of maternal nausea, vomiting, and hypotension compared to prompt administration post spinal anesthesia induction.
